news.title: The 10 best right-backs in world football RANKED: Who can challenge Hakimi?
news.lede: The title of world’s best right-back isn’t up for much debate, but the race for the remaining places is fiercely contested. Europe’s elite are packed with top-class options, with stars from Arsenal, Barcelona, Tottenham, Chelsea and Real Madrid among the standouts. Some thrive as attacking outlets, others excel defensively, while the very best manage to do both. Here’s our ranking of the 10 best right-backs in world football right now.

news.title: Ranking the 10 best midfielders in world football: Rodri, Rice, Vitinha…
news.lede: Who reigns supreme among world football’s central midfielders? The competition has rarely been fiercer, after superstar names from Barcelona, Manchester City and PSG strengthened their case at the 2026 World Cup. To be crystal clear, this list is reserved for proper midfielders, i.e. No.6s and No.8s – players you’d happily trust in a midfield two.

news.title: World Cup winner Llorente retires from Spain duty at 31
news.lede: World Cup winner Marcos Llorente announced his retirement from international football on Thursday, ending a Spain career that yielded 27 caps. The Atletico Madrid defender, 31, made his senior team debut for Spain in 2020 and was part of the squad that beat Argentina 1-0 to win the World Cup in July, although he remained on the bench in the final. "I realise that I’m still young and that, perhaps, if I continued to perform well, I’d still have years left to play in this jersey," Llorente wrote on Instagram. "I know many of you won’t understand this, and I probably wouldn’t have understood it either if I were looking at it from the outside.

news.title: ‘Exact same’: Socceroos boss’ penalty admission as 2030 World Cup contract surprisingly rejected
news.lede: Socceroos coach Tony Popovic has said he would not change his approach to Australia’s heartbreaking Round of 32 penalty shootout loss to Egypt at the FIFA World Cup, while revealing he knocked back a long-term contract from Football Australia. The Socceroos agonisingly exited the World Cup in July in Dallas when defenders Harry Souttar and Lucas Herrington missed penalties, while goalkeeper Mat Ryan failed to make a save after being brought on for the shootout. news.title: GSC & TGV Are Hosting a Watch Party for the World Cup Final With Free-Flow Popcorn & Drinks
news.lede: There’s just something special about watching football with a crowd. Whether it’s celebrating a last-minute winner, gasping over a missed chance, or debating every refereeing decision, the experience always feels more exciting when you’re surrounded by fellow fans. With the 2026 FIFA World Cup final looming, it’s the perfect time to gather your football-loving friends and soak in the atmosphere together. Exclusively for the final match, two of Malaysia's well-known cinema chains, GSC and TGV, are set to host live watch parties.

news.title: "Two months have passed since the World Cup, yet there is still no proper explanation..." Unprecedented 'suspension reprieve controversy' → Demand for official FIFA explanation
news.lede: Nearly two months have passed since the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA North America World Cup, but the fallout surrounding the unprecedented decision to grant a reprieve to the suspension of U.S. national team striker Paulinho Balogun has not subsided. British media outlet 'BBC' reported on the 8th (Korean time) that "the Royal Belgian Football Association (RBFA) is still demanding from FIFA a clear explanation as to why Polarin Balogun was allowed to play in their match during last year's World Cup Round of 16," and added that "they have requested that this matter be formally placed on the agenda for the next FIFA Council meeting scheduled for October." Anger toward FIFA has not yet subsided. The Belgian Football Association has officially declared that it will no longer support Gianni Infantino's bid for re-election as FIFA president.
